title: Decoding-Time KV Cache Eviction with Global Attention
one_line_claim: G-KV improves KV cache compression by combining local and historical attention scores to identify globally important tokens, enabling dynamic eviction during decoding.
method_summary: G-KV computes a global score for each token by combining attention from the current observation window with historical scores from preceding windows, using max, average, or summation operators. During generation, tokens are evicted based on these scores; post-training (RL with sparse attention masks and distillation) adapts the model to compressed cache constraints.

key_findings.finding: G-KV achieves SOTA across reasoning and coding benchmarks with significantly improved token retention efficiency. For AMC 23, achieves nearly 20% improvement under 512-token budget.
key_findings.quote: our method achieves SOTA performance across most budgets and benchmarks. The fewer the budget tokens, the greater the advantage of our method over others. For the AMC 23 benchmark, our approach achieves nearly a 20% improvement under a 512-token budget.

key_findings.finding: RL-Sparse training achieves pass@1 improvements of +6.01 to +7.81 on AMC 23 under different KV cache budgets.
key_findings.quote: RL-Sparse achieves the best performance across most settings, significantly outperforming models trained with the Full KV cache.

key_findings.finding: Tokens attended by the last observation window are not fully consistent with those attended by earlier windows; the inconsistency grows as fewer tokens are retained.
key_findings.quote: Observation 1: The tokens attended to by the last window are not fully consistent with those attended to by the earlier windows. As the number of retained tokens decreases, the inconsistency becomes more pronounced.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV cache compression and recognize that local attention patterns alone are insufficient to capture token importance.
differs_on: G-KV prevents failures through better compression heuristics (global scoring); HERALD detects imminent failures via logit-based ML prediction before they occur.
G-KV treats compression as an eviction problem; HERALD treats it as real-time hazard forecasting with a pre-onset horizon parameter.
G-KV uses attention patterns as primary signal; HERALD uses per-token log-probability distributions as XGBoost features.
